---
name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify a Domainry backend from accepted requirements or delivered frontend evidence. Use for metadata-first Domainry projects, frontend-to-Runtime replacement, Runtime integration, and full-stack defect routing. Keeps frontend evidence read-only except an explicitly authorized Data Exchange offline-export center.
---

# Domainry Builder V1

Each run owns one explicit Delivery Batch and follows exactly `requirements → model → apply → verify → done`. A batch is an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Keep one project-visible TODO at `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md`; copy [the template](assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md) only when it is absent, then resume its `Current stage`. Do not invent stages, state files, or continuation workflows.

The accepted product scope remains the baseline: never silently reduce it to an MVP. Put stable Requirement IDs and Feature keys in the current batch, record deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership, and include every shared resource or regression boundary affected by the batch. `done` means this batch is complete, not that deferred product scope was delivered.

Resolve this file's directory as `SKILL_ROOT` and set `DOMAINRY_CLI="$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"`. Use only that packaged CLI. The workflow has exactly five commands: `model capability`, `model plan`, `apply model`, `apply finalize`, and `verify`.

## requirements

Read [requirements and domain truth](references/requirements-and-domain-truth.md) and the [PRD template](assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md). Settle domain truth inside this stage for the current batch and its dependency closure: actors and scope; objects, relations, states, defaults, and retention; commands, transactions, idempotency, calculations, and external effects; Reports and offline export intent; schedules, notifications, files, and integrations. Any required human approve/reject wait is a Runtime Workflow requirement, not two synchronous Handler branches. Any required downloadable Report export is a governed `report_export_controls` plus offline Data Exchange requirement, not a Report permission alone.

When frontend source exists, inspect it as evidence, including API Mock adapters, handlers, fixtures, seeds, and mutation side effects. `frontend/**` is read-only except for the authorized export-center slice described below. Treat it as evidence, not authority for missing policy. Record frontend defects for owner `frontend`; do not hide them with backend workarounds. Preserve the accepted product baseline in `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` and record a traceable current-batch delta with stable Requirement IDs, sources, owners, acceptance results, Feature ownership and deferred scope. Do not advance while an unresolved choice changes current-batch observable behavior, authorization, money/units, an irreversible effect, or state flow.

## model

Read [backend model](references/backend-model.md), then use the [capability index](references/capabilities/README.md) to load only relevant contracts. Preserve the complete current desired state in `backend/model/*.json` and referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`; prefer one Feature per model file, and change only current-batch Features plus the declared shared-resource closure. Never edit `domain/**` or `.domainry/**`, and never emit compiler-owned `capability_assembly`, standalone Permission definitions, versions, ownership, or seed metadata. Author each ordinary Role directly as an array of exact `<permission_key>;<data_scope>` grants.

Classify every writable Object as either plain `direct_crud`, or `action_only` plus a source-owned Handler for any named, conditional, derived, state-changing, side-effecting, or cross-record command. Do not author new Automation. A human approval must be an enabled Workflow graph with an approval task, authorized assignee resolver, explicit approved and rejected branches, and terminal Action effects; standalone approve/reject Handlers are not the waiting process. Reports use `object_sql_v1`; every required export also authors the Blueprint `report_export_controls` closure (bounded rows, audit/download Objects and mappings, requester-owned grants, assurance/masking when required) while Runtime Report and Data Exchange own execution.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--key <category>]
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

`model plan` performs one immutable load of the complete current model, validates the whole cross-resource draft, derives capability and authorization closure, persists deterministic diagnostics/provenance, and reports the Ledger change set. A Delivery Batch is not a loader or apply filter. Confirm that every create, update and delete belongs to the batch or its declared impact closure; repair the named owner and rerun. Once valid, keep the model unchanged while reviewing removals and evolution-sensitive changes.

## apply

Read [project mutation](references/project-mutation.md), then apply the reviewed model:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module>
```

Retain its immutable implementation packet. Read [ownership and extensions](references/ownership-and-extensions.md), then implement only the project-owned backend source and paired tests declared by that packet. For a selected custom Connector, request its focused context with `model capability --connector-context <connector.provider>` immediately before implementation. Never edit generated source, manifests, receipts, caches, journals, or managed Runtime state.

The only frontend mutation exception is a Data Exchange offline-export center for an exportable Object SQL Report when `Frontend mutation scope: integration_authorized`; follow [its contract](references/frontend-offline-report-export.md). Otherwise report the owner gap.

Run focused tests, then finalize every delivered Handler and Connector:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply finalize --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

`apply finalize` enforces source call-site contracts, including guarded `ConditionalUpdate`; do not add manual grep gates. Run the affected backend test set before advancing.

## verify

Read [evidence levels](references/evidence-levels.md), [verification](references/verification.md), and [Runtime integration](references/backend-runtime.md). Every current-batch business flow and affected regression boundary needs a complete project-owned case with explicit preconditions, ordered actions, and a terminal durable result; denial cases also prove unchanged state. Unchanged flows may reuse only current baseline evidence. Run the highest-risk changed case against the managed Runtime before broader flow verification.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --address 127.0.0.1:<port>
```

`verify` runs structural checks and the complete backend test tree, packages the exact source, proves healthy start and same-cohort restart, then leaves the managed Runtime stopped. `backend/tests/businessflow` is a black-box Runtime package: it may use published Runtime HTTP/client operations but never import project Handlers, generated capability/data fakes, or database drivers. Treat Runtime identifiers and principal/context values as opaque. A shared login, health, read, or Action-catalog probe does not prove another named flow; each claimed Runtime case must execute its own ordered Runtime journey and read back its terminal durable result. Approval cases start the Workflow, observe the task, prove unauthorized denial, decide both branches, and read back process/task/business state. Export cases query and prepare the governed Report export, follow the requester-owned Data Exchange job to completion/download, and prove another actor is denied. Verify only requirement-observable denial, scope, conflict, rollback, replay, restart, worker, Report, export, file, notification, and provider behavior. Do not create a second evidence ledger or generic acceptance runner.

## done

Set `Current stage: done` only when every current-batch finding is resolved and current receipts, tests, durable observations, and Runtime identity support the claim. Report batch identity and scope, delivery identity, changed files, tests, Runtime result, highest evidence level, deferred Requirement IDs, and explicit limitations without claiming deferred product work is complete.

Project-owned edits are limited to requirements/TODO evidence, declarative model/SQL, backend source/tests, and the authorized export-center exception. Recoverable failures stay in the current stage: repair the responsible owner and rerun the same direct command.

# Requirements and domain truth

Use only for the `requirements` TODO section. Produce the accepted backend dependency PRD and freeze domain facts before capability discovery. Do not load model, apply, verification, or acceptance authority at this stage.

## Backend dependency PRD

Preserve the full accepted product demand as the requirements baseline. For a new project, complete replacement, or existing project increment, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`, or record an equivalent traceable current-batch delta that references the unchanged accepted baseline. Never silently reduce product demand to an MVP.

One Delivery Batch may implement an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Record its stable Requirement IDs, planned Feature keys, baseline delivery/model identity, allowed shared-resource changes and affected regression boundary. Requirements outside the batch remain explicit deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership; `done` closes only the batch. A Feature slice must be dependency-closed: include any shared Role, entrypoint, Object, Action, Report, lifecycle or authorization change required for its behavior to be valid and verifiable.

Settle domain truth completely for the current batch and dependency closure before capability discovery. Deferred slices need enough stable identity and ownership to remain visible, but their unresolved details do not block this batch unless they change its observable result, authorization, amount/unit semantics, irreversible effect, or state flow. A later batch reuses the accepted baseline and resolves its own delta instead of rewriting unrelated requirements.

A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as `<doc> §N`. If one section states a rule completely, cite it rather than restating it. A reference-mode PRD still carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section.

Read frontend evidence, when present, in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/handlers and fixtures/seeds; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Requirements inspection is read-only. Mock or visible behavior proves demand or a current assumption, not a business rule without higher-precedence evidence.

When the frontend is already implemented, do not stop at API method names or TypeScript types. Search for every API dependency's Mock implementation, including request handlers, success/error responses, fixture collections, seeded identities, mutation side effects, generated identifiers, relation keys, enum/status values, timestamps, totals, and nested objects. Reconcile those concrete values with component reads and writes. Add any evidenced missing object, field, relation, lifecycle state, query shape, or representative worked example to the PRD, with its exact source path and an appropriate classification. Preserve conflicts and optionality: Mock-only fields remain `recommended` or `open` unless higher-precedence evidence confirms them, and decorative/test-only values do not become domain facts.

Use this precedence while preserving every conflict:

1. explicit current user decision;
2. latest accepted requirement or design contract;
3. latest implemented frontend behavior;
4. typed API and Mock semantics;
5. frontend tests;
6. legacy/reference implementation.

Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`. Extract actors, journeys, observable success, objects, fields, relations, queries, commands, states, permissions/scopes, errors/conflicts, calculations, transactions/idempotency, external effects, and presentation-only behavior. Every write operation names authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof.

Build one traceability row per in-scope requirement: `demand evidence → requirement ID → Feature key → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Account for every backend-bound typed API operation and route touched by the batch; reference the accepted baseline for unchanged rows and preserve explicit dispositions for deferred rows. Matrix cells are phrases; do not repeat table facts in prose.

## Critical ambiguity

Classify every unresolved choice before capability selection. Only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring, and only for the smallest affected slice.

| Decision class | Boundary | Handling | Blocks model? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `business_blocker` | At least two concrete incompatible choices remain, and selecting one changes an explicitly required observable result, authorization allow/deny, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow | Name the choices, affected requirements/model items, and obtain current user or accepted requirement authority | Yes, smallest slice only |
| `contract_discovery` | Runtime-owned formal code, canonical identity/context source, or accepted-fact-to-capability mapping | Defer discovery to the typed client/fixed capability contract; record a Foundation/Runtime gap if absent | No |
| `safe_implementation_decision` | Reversible technical choice preserving the accepted invariant | Defer to the published standard or record one conservative default and evolution path | No |
| `product_follow_up` | Product preference with a fallback that preserves required results | Record assumption, owner, fallback, excluded acceptance scope, and review trigger | No |

Security/privacy omissions default to least privilege, sensitive by default, and no export. An explicit broader-disclosure requirement remains a `business_blocker` until its authorization boundary is confirmed.

Use these nonblocking defaults without inventing product rules:

- Explicit exact decimals, comparisons, or sums do not require absent optional currency/unit/range metadata; block only a comparison/conversion slice where incompatible units change the required result.
- Explicit asynchronous approval may use an independent approval Object while the host remains unchanged until the terminal effect; missing edit/cancel/resubmit preferences are follow-ups.
- An explicitly immutable resource with no required business-role read needs no invented read actor; prove creation through a formal admin/seed path or persistence evidence.
- Weekday/morning intent with no timezone/holiday preference uses deterministic deployment timezone and standard weekday cron; block only explicit incompatible calendar outcomes.

## Domain truth design

Freeze domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement. When requirements contain calculations, historical facts, settlement, correction, or reversal, read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) once and close its ownership, persistence, snapshot, trace, correction, and consumer decisions.

Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, define the write-side atomic action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its reports.

Before capability discovery, settle only the model-visible Report facts: the business question, Object SQL source of truth, parameters and defaults, result columns and meanings, authorization/audience, and whether export is required. Report query transport and export execution are Runtime-owned and stay out of the project model and PRD.

Every required Report export defaults to an offline Data Exchange job. When the project owns a frontend, the PRD also records the export-center route/audience and the actor-visible job-list/download outcome. If the active typed Runtime Client lacks the actor-owned Data Exchange export-job list, record a Data Exchange owner gap instead of inventing a route or browser-local list.

Verify the authorized Object SQL result, out-of-scope denial, offline job submission, actor-owned job-list visibility, and completed-file download when export is required. Do not turn Runtime execution internals into project acceptance cases.

Record any explicitly required current-database query-plan evidence and driver (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, or `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`) as a business-flow verification obligation. Capability schemas are resolved during model routing; do not manufacture a separate platform gate catalog or case inventory.

# M1 Benchmark:销售线索 CRM 需求规格

本文档是 benchmark 的唯一需求输入。评分对照 golden-checklist(agent 不可见)。

## 业务背景

一家 B2B 公司的销售团队管理线索(lead)到成交客户(customer)的全流程:销售录入并跟进线索,大额转化需销售总监审批,团队按部门划分数据边界,管理层看漏斗报表并导出。

## 组织与角色

- 销售分属**部门**(至少两个部门:华东区、华北区),存在汇报线。
- **sales_rep(销售)**:录入/跟进自己名下的线索;可见范围=本部门线索;发起转化。
- **sales_director(销售总监)**:全部门可见;审批大额转化;查看/导出漏斗报表。

## 功能需求

### 线索管理
1. 线索字段:公司名(必填)、联系人、联系电话、预计金额(精确金额,两位小数)、来源(select:官网/展会/转介绍/外呼)、状态、负责人(销售)、部门、创建/更新时间。
2. 线索状态机:`new → contacted → qualified → converted / lost`;`qualified` 可标记 `lost`;`converted`、`lost` 为终态,不可再转换。
3. 销售创建线索(初始 new,负责人=本人,部门=本人部门);可更新自己名下线索的联系人/电话/预计金额/来源。
4. 跟进(contacted)与合格判定(qualified)由负责人执行;状态只能沿定义的转换变化。
5. 线索创建幂等(相同幂等键重复提交只建一条)。

### 转化与审批(核心业务)
6. 负责人对 `qualified` 线索发起**转化**:预计金额 < 100000 时直接转化;≥ 100000 时必须进入**审批流**,由 sales_director 审批。
7. 审批通过:线索进入 `converted`,并在**同一事务**中创建 `customer` 客户记录(承接公司名/联系人/金额/来源线索引用);审批拒绝:线索回到 `qualified` 并记录拒绝原因。
8. 转化必须幂等:同一线索重复发起转化不产生第二个客户。
9. 审批结果(通过/拒绝)以站内通知发给发起的销售。
10. 客户记录只读(任何角色不可更新/删除客户;修正走新流程,本期不做)。

### 数据边界
11. 销售的线索可见范围 = **本部门**(同部门同事的线索可见,跨部门不可见);更新/状态操作仅限**自己名下**。
12. 总监全量可见。
13. 所有状态变化与转化审批留审计。

### 跟进提醒(定时)
14. 每天早上(工作日)由**定时任务**扫描:`contacted` 状态超过 7 天未变化的线索,给负责人发站内提醒(每条线索每天最多提醒一次)。

### 报表与导出
15. 总监可见**漏斗报表**:按状态统计线索数与预计金额合计;销售无权查看。
16. 总监可**导出线索明细 CSV**(带当前权限过滤);导出必须走受控导出通道(有界、审计、requester 专属)。
17. 线索列表服务端有界分页。

### 导航与验收
18. 两角色登录 Business Workspace 后菜单与权限一致(销售:我的线索;总监:全部线索、报表)。
19. 提供两个部门 × 各 1 名销售 + 1 名总监的非人类验收身份,以及覆盖所有状态、两个部门、含 ≥100000 与 <100000 金额的种子线索(≥6 条),保证每条需求可在真实 Runtime 验证。

## 范围限定

仅 Business Workspace;无 Consumer Portal、无外部连接器;金额计算只做求和,不涉及分成/结算。

## 公开业务旅程追踪 ID

以下 ID 是需求输入的一部分，不包含 evaluator 的隐藏断言。`docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`
必须建立需求 → flow ID → 测试名/路径追踪；`backend/tests/businessflow/` 下对应的顶层 Go 测试名
必须以 `TestBFxx` 开头。同一 ID 可以拆成多个测试，但每个分支都要验证持久化终态和失败后的状态不变性。

- `BF01`：销售创建线索、创建幂等、本人更新、负责人状态推进，以及同部门非负责人写入拒绝。
- `BF02`：小额线索从 qualified 直接转化、只创建一个只读客户，并验证重放幂等。
- `BF03`：大额线索发起审批并由总监通过；线索转化与客户创建同事务，发起人收到通知。
- `BF04`：大额审批拒绝；线索回到 qualified、拒绝原因与通知可读，且不创建客户。
- `BF05`：两个部门销售的同部门可见/跨部门不可见、总监全量可见、有界分页和角色菜单差异。
- `BF06`：工作日逾期跟进提醒，包含单日去重及重启后结果保持。
- `BF07`：总监漏斗报表的状态计数与金额合计正确，销售访问被拒绝。
- `BF08`：总监受控 CSV 导出完成、审计、requester 专属可见与下载；销售发起导出被拒绝。

## 1. Scope and evidence rules

- Backend scope:
- Managed Runtime database driver: `cohort_default` / `sqlite` / `mysql` / `postgres` (use an explicit driver only when the requirement authority fixes the later Runtime cohort)
- Verification database driver: `same_as_managed_runtime` (never require a second engine; every business-flow case and query-profile row must use the managed Runtime cohort's driver)
- Source document(s) and citation scheme (reference mode):
- Requirements evidence closure: non-empty this PRD + root `requirements.md` when present + non-derived `frontend/**` evidence when `frontend/src/**` exists; otherwise immutable external reference/snapshot recorded here
- Explicitly excluded frontend-only scope:
- Accepted baseline reused by this delta:
- Current-batch dependency closure:
- Deferred product scope preserved by this batch:
- Evidence precedence or approved exceptions:
- Known conflicts:
- Completed-frontend Mock inventory (API operation → handler/adapter → fixture/seed → PRD object/fields/relations/states; record `none found` only after searching):

Requirement classification values: `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, `legacy_reference`. Unresolved decisions separately use `business_blocker`, `contract_discovery`, `safe_implementation_decision`, or `product_follow_up` per `requirements-and-domain-truth.md#critical-ambiguity`; only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring.

## 2. Actors, roles, and journeys

| Journey ID | Actor / role | Entry route | Preconditions | Steps and backend interactions | Observable success | Failure / recovery | Classification | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

# Foundation capability index

Read only the documents selected here, but read all matches before authoring the compact backend model. These files explain how to consume current owners; the compiler expands the full Ledger/Blueprint and source-owner contracts plus Runtime validators remain authoritative.

- Account, login, member/customer profile, Object-UX profile binding (`identity_relation_field`, `required_binding_key`), platform-owned profile fields: [identity/account/profile](identity-account-and-profile.md).
- Company/region/store/department/team/warehouse nodes, parent unit, organization paths, and organization data scope: [organization units](organization-unit.md).
- User personnel facts, primary organization, direct manager (`manager_user_id`), and reporting path: [Identity User and reporting line](identity-user-and-reporting-line.md).
- Customers, suppliers, contacts, consent, and other non-login business subjects are ordinary project-owned domain objects unless they are a one-to-one Identity business Profile; there is no Party foundation module.
- Approval, CC, or escalation involving organizations, managers, roles, or record-selected users: read organization, Identity User reporting line, and the assignee-resolver decision matrix in [workflow](workflow.md) together before choosing a resolver.
- Object, field, relation, record mutation, guarded state transitions, or required lifecycle immutability: read [records](records-fields-and-relations.md), [CRUD/state machine](crud-and-state-machine.md), and [actions/transactions](actions-and-transactions.md). These references enforce the only new write-owner choice: plain Runtime CRUD, or `action_only` plus a source-owned Handler for business logic. Prefer inline `select` values; only read the Dictionary subsection in records when one controlled vocabulary is genuinely reused and centrally localized or ordered. Single-Object list/search/filter/sort uses Runtime Records queries from frontend source and has no separate backend-model resource; use [reports](reports.md) only for aggregates, joins, snapshots, or export.
- Roles, RBAC, field/reference/export policy, data scope, actor claims, RLS predicate: [permissions](permissions-and-data-scope.md). Standard role/scope/claim pairings for member portal, staff back office, multi-store, cross-organization customer service, or team-scoped account administration: [RBAC cookbook](rbac-and-data-scope-cookbook.md).
- Headquarters-managed tenant/store creation, initial administrator, baseline tenant records, and roles copied into every new workspace: [workspace provisioning](workspace-provisioning.md). Read it together with [permissions](permissions-and-data-scope.md).
- Compiler-derived behavior ownership (`runtime_crud`, `runtime_system_action`, `business_handler`, `automation_before`, `automation_after`, `workflow`, `scheduler`): [behavior owner decision](behavior-owner-decision.md).
- Timed work: [scheduler](scheduler.md). Object SQL analytics and offline Data Exchange export: [reports](reports.md); when export is required, also read [offline Report export frontend](../frontend-offline-report-export.md). Business audit-event export: [permissions](permissions-and-data-scope.md) together with [backend Runtime integration](../backend-runtime.md); it is a separate Runtime report source.
- Model reasoning, structured analysis, durable AI tasks, approval-gated proposals, Workflow Agent nodes, global assistant entrypoints, service execution identity, Tool Gateway authorization, retry/cancel/recovery: [Agents and Agent Tasks](agents-and-agent-tasks.md). Read it with [workflow](workflow.md) for an `agent_task` node, [actions](actions-and-transactions.md) for proposed or allowed effects, and [reports](reports.md) for governed analytics.
- Personal Inbox, unread badge, actionable station messages, notification preferences, and the boundary between user-impacting events and operational errors: [in-app notifications](in-app-notifications.md). Read it with [backend Runtime integration](../backend-runtime.md) whenever Business Workspace or Consumer Portal requirements include a notification center.
- External effects, provider/operation discovery, connection binding, connector capability gap: [connectors](connectors.md).
- Named business journeys and entrypoint coverage: [business entrypoints](business-entrypoints.md). Frontend navigation, routes, layout, list configuration, interaction, and login presentation stay in frontend source.
- Backend-model starter template and composable Ledger patterns: `templates/README.md`.
## Task profile minimum reading sets

Pick exactly one profile, then add only capability documents matched above.

- New project initial Feature slice or full delivery: this index, documents routed by the current-batch dependency closure, [domainry-plane](../domainry-plane.md), [project-mutation](../project-mutation.md), [backend-model](../backend-model.md), [authorization](../authorization.md), and [backend Runtime integration](../backend-runtime.md).
- Existing project Feature increment or cross-cutting evolution: this index restricted to the changed Feature and affected shared-capability closure, [domainry-plane](../domainry-plane.md), [project-mutation](../project-mutation.md), and [backend-model](../backend-model.md) when metadata changes.
- Handler repair: run the ordinary model/apply path so `apply model` produces the current implementation packet, then use [project-mutation](../project-mutation.md), [ownership-and-extensions](../ownership-and-extensions.md), and [behavior owner decision](behavior-owner-decision.md). There is no separate repair-context route.

Do not use raw `curl`, `jq`, or repository search merely to rediscover these foundation facts. Use bounded formal contract commands when an exact release-bound symbol is needed.

# Backend model files

`backend/model/*.json` is the only model-authored backend metadata input. The
model writes business differences; Plane expands every structural default into
the complete Ledger, Blueprint, authorization, Runtime Manifest, version and
hash contracts. Never edit `domain/**`, rendered Blueprints, or `.domainry/**`
by hand.

## V3 file contract

The only top-level fields are `project` and `modules`. Exactly one file declares
`project`; modules and features may be split across files, but a Feature key and
a resource identity may each be declared only once across the whole model.

```json
{
  "project": {
    "id": "item_submission",
    "name": "事项提交"
  },
  "modules": {
    "core": {
      "features": {
        "item_lifecycle": {
          "requirement": {
            "statement": "操作员可以提交待处理事项。",
            "acceptance": [
              "提交成功后产生持久结果。",
              "失败时不得产生部分数据。"
            ]
          },
          "objects": {
            "item": {
              "fields": {
                "name": "text!",
                "status": "select![pending:待提交|submitted:已提交]=pending"
              }
            },
            "item_submission": {
              "fields": {
                "source_record_id": "relation!->item",
                "status": "select![recorded:已记录]"
              }
            }
          },
          "roles": {
            "item_operator": ["item.read;all", "item.submit;owner"]
          },
          "actions": {
            "item.submit": {
              "kind": "record_operation",
              "handler": {
                "reason": "必须原子更新事项并创建提交记录",
                "access": {
                  "item": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
                  "item_submission": ["create"]
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Delivery batches and file ownership

Whole-model validation does not require whole-product implementation. The files
currently present under `backend/model/*.json` are the complete desired-state
baseline for this delivery. A Delivery Batch is an authoring and verification
scope, not a loader or apply filter: preserve every previously applied model
file, then add or update only the batch's Feature files and declared
shared-resource closure. `model plan` and `apply model` continue to load and
validate the complete current model atomically.

Prefer `00-project.json` plus one Feature per descriptively named model file.
Several files may declare different Features under the same module. A Role,
entrypoint or other cross-cutting resource still has one owning Feature/file;
when it supports multiple Features, declare those stable keys through the
resource `requirements` override instead of repeating the resource.

The Feature key is also its Requirement identity. Moving one intact Feature to
another file does not change Ledger identity, but splitting or renaming a
Feature creates new Requirement identities, relinks affected resources and may
delete the old Requirement. Review that change with `model plan`; never treat it
as a mechanical file edit. For an already-applied oversized Feature, a valid
staged migration may retain the old Feature as a requirement-only umbrella,
move one resource group per batch to a new Feature, and temporarily link those
resources to both Requirement keys. Retire the umbrella only in a later,
explicitly reviewed destructive batch when it no longer represents accepted
product demand.

The V2 `items -> module -> kind -> item -> payload -> emits` envelope is not
accepted. Do not author `kind`, `status`, `depends_on`, `decisions`,
`requirement_keys`, `contract_version`, `capability_assembly`, or internal
Ledger item names. This project is not released yet, so there is no legacy
format fallback.

## Feature ownership and traceability

Every resource inside a Feature inherits that Feature's requirement. Plane
creates the requirement Ledger item, resource dependencies and behavior links.
Only a resource shared by multiple Features declares an override:

```json
{
  "item": {
    "requirements": ["item_lifecycle", "audit_requirement"],
    "fields": {"name": "text!"}
  }
}
```

`requirement` contains only `statement` and optional non-empty `acceptance`.
Behavior owner tuples and the no-executable reason are compiler output.

## Keyed identities everywhere

Every schema array whose item has a stable identity is authored as a keyed
object. The compiler sorts it, injects `key`, `id`, `object_key`, `path`, or
`connection_key` as required, and emits the strongly typed array. This includes
Objects, Fields, Roles, Actions, dictionary items, report parameters/result
columns, notification variables, Workflow inputs/nodes/edges, Automation
instructions and Agent resources. Repeating the identity inside a value or
using an identity-bearing array fails model loading.

Examples:

```json
{"input_fields": {"comment": "long_text!"}}
```

```json
{
  "graph": {
    "nodes": {
      "start": {"type": "trigger"},
      "finish": {"type": "action"}
    },
    "edges": {
      "start_finish": {"source": "start", "target": "finish"}
    }
  }
}
```

State transitions use their directed edge as identity, so duplicate edges are
structurally impossible:

```json
{"transitions": {"draft->submitted": "item.submit", "submitted->archived": {"workflow": "item.archive"}}}
```

Open maps remain maps. In particular Agent `input_schema`/`output_schema`
properties, Action/Workflow bindings, connector configuration and other
business dictionaries are not mistaken for resource arrays.

## Field string DSL

Object Fields, Action `input`/`output`, Workflow inputs, Report SQL parameters
and notification variables use the same compact base grammar:

```text
<type>[!][->target][value[:label]|...][=default][;modifier[=value]]...
```

### Complete type and modifier quick reference

This is the single copyable reference for the field DSL. It contains every
supported field type and every Object-field modifier; capability references
should link here instead of repeating the table.

```json
{
  "active": "boolean=true",
  "amount": "currency!;precision=19;scale=2;currency=CNY;rounding=half_even",
  "effective_date": "date!",
  "starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03T09:00:00+08:00",
  "contact_email": "email!;max_length=254",
  "quantity": "integer!;min=1;max=999",
  "remark": "long_text;min_length=1;max_length=500;localized",
  "score": "number;min=0;max=100",
  "discount_rate": "percent;precision=5;scale=2;rounding=half_even",
  "contact_phone": "phone;pattern=^\\+[1-9][0-9]{7,14}$",
  "customer_id": "relation!->customer;cardinality=many_to_one;on_delete=restrict;inverse=invoices",
  "status": "select![draft:草稿|done:完成]=draft",
  "business_no": "text!;unique;indexed",
  "website": "url",
  "assignee": "user",
  "category": "select!;dictionary=case_category",
  "risk_level": "select!;value_domain=risk_level"
}
```

- `!` means required.
- `relation` requires `->target` and never accepts a default.
- `select` requires a non-empty, unique stable vocabulary. Labels default from
  the stable value when omitted.
- Supported Object modifiers are `unique`, `indexed`, `localized`,
  `min_length`, `max_length`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `precision`, `scale`,
  `currency`, `rounding`, `cardinality`, `on_delete`, `inverse`, `dictionary`,
  and `value_domain`.
- Unknown types/modifiers, duplicates, invalid values, out-of-vocabulary
  defaults and context-inapplicable modifiers fail closed.

Common repairs are local to the rejected field string:

| Rejected | Use | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"customer_id": "relation!"` | `"customer_id": "relation!->customer"` | A relation requires its target. |
| `"status": "select!"` | `"status": "select![draft\|done]"` | Select needs exactly one vocabulary source. |
| `"status": "select![draft];dictionary=status"` | Choose inline options or `dictionary`, not both. | Vocabulary sources are exclusive. |
| `"amount": "currency;precision=2;scale=3"` | `"amount": "currency;precision=19;scale=2"` | Scale cannot exceed precision. |
| `"starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03 09:00"` | `"starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03T09:00:00+08:00"` | Datetime defaults use RFC3339. |

The CLI rejects an invalid string during model loading and reports the stable
diagnostic code, exact JSON path, field key and repair facts. Fix that string;
do not replace the compact field map with generated full field arrays.

Plane expands Object fields to `key`, `name`, `type`, `required`, `config`,
`validation`, labeled `options`, `unique` and `default_value`. Human-readable
names default from stable keys (`item_submission` -> `Item Submission`). Object
descriptions also receive a deterministic non-empty default; provide explicit
text only when it carries real domain meaning.

Action fields use the same strings. Object-only modifiers on an Action field
are consistency assertions: Plane derives a same-key field reference to the
Action's owning Object and rejects a missing, differently typed or differently
constrained Object field. This preserves the named type/precision contract
without exposing `source_object_key` or `source_field_key` to the model.

## Actions and source-owned Handlers

An Action key is exactly `<object_key>.<action_key>`; Plane derives
`object_key`, the default name, audit metadata, same-key Permission and empty
contracts. The model decides `kind`, allowed business roles, business fields,
preconditions and whether a source-owned Handler is needed.

```json
{
  "invoice.approve": {
    "kind": "record_operation",
    "input": {"comment": "long_text!", "effective_date": "date!"},
    "output": {"status": "select![approved|rejected]"},
    "handler": {
      "reason": "Approval updates the invoice and durable decision atomically",
      "access": {
        "invoice": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
        "approval_decision": ["create"]
      },
      "connector_calls": {"accounting_primary": "enqueue_invoice_sync"}
    }
  }
}
```

`handler.reason` is the only authored capability-gap/rationale statement.
Plane derives owner, trigger, scope, atomicity, rollback semantics, involved
Objects, read/write sets and transaction requirement. Do not author
`authorization`, `payload_fields`, `handler.data_access`, `handler.output`,
`audit_event`, empty defaults, or behavior tuples.

Do not put protocol or infrastructure identifiers in Action input: `id`,
`request_id`, `trace_id`, `correlation_id`, `idempotency_key`, `workspace_id`,
`principal_id`, `record_id`, `route_id`, `tenant_id`, `session_id`,
`database_id`, `db_id`, and `row_id` are rejected. Record targets come from the
Action route, idempotency from `Idempotency-Key`, request identity from Runtime,
and new technical IDs from backend code. Stable business numbers remain
legitimate business fields.

## Roles, data scope and write ownership

Roles contain exact Permission grants, and every grant carries its own scope:

```json
{"reviewer": ["case.read;org", "case.approve;owner", "case_attachment.read;owner"]}
```

The only scope values are `all`, `owner`, `org`, `org_child`, and
`target_org`. The Role's same-key Action Permission is the only authored
allowlist. Plane reverse-derives `authorization.allowed_roles`, registers the
Action Permission definition, and never invents a Role grant or scope. Authoring
`Action.roles` is rejected as a duplicate source.

Object write policy is compiler-owned:

- an Object written by a Handler is `action_only` and has no Runtime CRUD
  behavior;
- every other Object is `direct_crud` and receives a Runtime CRUD behavior;
- a direct create/update/delete/restore Role permission or entrypoint mutation
  on a Handler-written Object is a blocking ownership conflict.

Plane expands Role grants into one scoped data-permission container per declared Role/Object.
That container is compiler-owned: the model declares each exact
Permission and scope once as `roles.<role>[] = "<permission_key>;<data_scope>"` and never repeats the
expanded Object policy.

Never author `config.write_policy`, role-level `data_scope`, `scope_overrides`,
`data_permissions` or `reference_permissions`. Handler roles use their explicit
same-key Action grant without receiving direct CRUD mutation permissions.

## Relation reference input

A `relation->target` field is also the complete model input for a reusable
reference selector. Plane derives an exact reference policy only when the role
can write the source Object and read the target Object; duplicate
source/field/target policies collapse to one stable identity.

The frontend calls
`GET /records/{sourceObjectKey}/fields/{relationFieldKey}/options`
with the raw user `query`. It never supplies a target Object, display field,
permission, SQL wildcard or `LIKE` expression. Runtime resolves the relation,
enforces the reference and target row/field policies, escapes `%`, `_` and the
escape character, then creates a parameterized case-insensitive contains
predicate. The component renders only the returned `{"id":"…","name":"…"}`
items.

## Report SQL

Prefer one source-owned file instead of an escaped SQL string:

```json
{"reports": {
  "part_usage": {
    "audience_roles": ["report_reader"],
    "object_sql_v1": {
      "sql_file": "backend/reports/part_usage.sql",
      "source_objects": ["part"],
      "parameters": {"status": "select![active|inactive]"},
      "result_schema": {
        "part_no": {"type": "text", "kind": "dimension"}
      }
    }
  }
}}
```

The path must be exactly `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`, canonical,
project-local and non-symlink. Plane normalizes line endings, hashes the source
and embeds SQL in the full Runtime contract. `sql_file` and `sql` are mutually
exclusive.

## Empty values and commands

Omit empty strings, arrays and objects. Omit absent `input`, `output`,
`permissions`, `config`, `preconditions` and optional collections; Plane
creates required empty internal structures. `false` and `0` remain legal only
when they are deliberate business values.

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <module> [--allow-destructive]
```

`model plan` is the no-HTTP repair loop. It runs the same loader, Ledger graph,
authoring checks, Project Contract projection, Runtime Manifest compiler and
source-owner validators used by apply. `apply model` atomically converges the
generated Ledger; an item absent from the model is a destructive deletion and
requires `--allow-destructive`.

Capability assembly remains progressive: choose from bounded summaries, load
only selected focused definitions, and let Plane compile ownership, module
closure and digests. Never author or cache a capability assembly in the model.

`templates/backend-model-handler-minimal/model.json.tmpl` is the directly
loadable two-Object Handler starter.

# Organization unit

Identity owns one organization tree. Company, region, store, department, team
and warehouse are node types in that tree, not separate project hierarchies.
Runtime consumes Identity-expanded organization and reporting descendants.

Projects may store a business relation to the canonical external Object:

```json
{"fields": {"org_id": "relation->identity_organization_unit"}}
```

Do not target retired department entities or copy parent, path, ancestor,
manager or depth columns. A domain-specific store/warehouse Object is valid
only for additional business data and relates back to the Identity node.

Every exact Role Permission carries its own explicit scope:

```json
{
  "roles": {
    "operator": ["service_request.read;org_child"]
  }
}
```

The only scopes are `all`, `owner`, `org`, `org_child`, and `target_org`.
`target_org` uses the trusted support-organization scope supplied by Identity.
Omitting the exact Permission denies access; do not add custom scopes or predicates.

Every business record receives Runtime-owned `owner_user_id` and
`owner_org_id`. Do not declare them, `scope_owner`, organization expansion or
reporting paths in the backend model. Runtime initializes ownership from the
trusted principal and Identity evaluates the current tree on each request.
# Identity user and reporting line

> **TL;DR** — Identity User itself owns the person's primary organization placement, personnel facts, direct manager, and reporting path. There is no separate Workforce profile or assignment model.

## Ownership

`domainry-identity` owns `identity_user`. Besides login identity and account status, the same User record owns:

- `org_id` — the user's one primary organization unit;
- `manager_user_id` — the user's direct manager, referencing another User;
- `reporting_path` — Identity-derived, persisted reporting-tree path;
- `worker_no`, `worker_type`, `work_status`, `start_date`, and `end_date` — personnel facts when required.

The organization tree and reporting tree are independent. Moving an organization node changes organization paths. Changing `manager_user_id` changes the user's reporting path and atomically rewrites descendant reporting paths. An organization unit does not carry a leader user ID, and no organization node is created for an individual person.

## Blueprint boundary

Runtime exposes `identity_user` as an external relation target. A project may reference a User where a business record needs an owner, applicant, operator, or approver. It must not declare a second employee/personnel table merely to duplicate Identity-owned fields.

The Blueprint never authors Identity operational state: no `identity_bootstrap`, users, personnel rows, organization units, managers, credentials, or live role assignments. Provision those through Identity module/SaaS APIs and fixtures.

Business-specific facts still belong to business objects. For example, commission grade, training certification, shift preference, and domain-specific qualifications may live in a one-to-one business Profile related to `identity_user`; the Profile must not copy the User fields listed above.

## Workflow manager resolution

`manager_of` reads a user-valued record field and resolves that User's `manager_user_id`. `initiator_manager` resolves the actual process initiator's `manager_user_id`. Runtime ignores missing or inactive manager accounts and applies the node's `empty_assignee_policy`. Neither resolver infers a manager from organization membership, role name, job title, or an organization-unit leader.

## Data authorization

Roles grant exact Permissions, each with its own `data_scope`. Users are not separately granted organizations through role-to-organization or user-to-organization assignment tables. Runtime stores stable `owner_user_id` and `owner_org_id` system columns on each business record. Identity supplies the current organization tree for `org_child` and the trusted support-organization tree for `target_org`; neither policy reads a path copied into the business record. Reporting-line membership is not a separate authoring scope.

## Authority and limits

`domainry-identity` owns User persistence, reporting-tree validation, and personnel lifecycle facts. `domainry-identity-sdk` owns identity projection and authorization contracts. Runtime consumes User facts for workflow resolution and policy enforcement; Plane only publishes business metadata and project-role policy.
# Permissions and data scope

Code-owned resources define the stable permission catalog. The backend model
defines application roles and business scope decisions. Identity owns users,
credentials, live assignments and principal resolution.

## Compact role input

Roles are keyed by stable identity. Each exact Permission grant carries its own
data visibility decision:

```json
{"roles": {
  "work_operator": [
    "work_item.read;owner",
    "work_item.export;org",
    "work_item_attachment.read;org_child;audit_denial"
  ]
}}
```

When a Role also needs metadata, use the extended object form and put the same
grant strings under `grants`:

```json
{"roles": {
  "work_operator": {
    "grants": [
      "work_item.read;owner",
      "work_item.export;org",
      "work_item_attachment.read;org_child;audit_denial"
    ],
    "field_permissions": {
      "work_item.private_note": {
        "read": true,
        "write": false,
        "export": false,
        "masked": true,
        "reason": "Private notes are not exportable"
      }
    }
  }
}}
```

`name` defaults from the role key. Every array item is an exact Permission key
and one of `all`, `owner`, `org`, `org_child`, or `target_org`, separated by a
semicolon. Append `;audit_denial` only when denied attempts must be audited.
Duplicate Permission keys are invalid. `grants` may be omitted from the extended
object when no explicit business grant exists.

The backend model must not declare role-level `data_scope`, `scope_overrides`,
`record_scope`, `data_permissions`,
`reference_permissions`, a root `permissions` collection, accounts, sessions,
users, assignments, or menu assignments.

## Compiler authorization closure

Plane preserves each authored scoped grant and validates the complete
authorization closure:

- `Action` -> the same-key Permission definition registered by Runtime;
- Role same-key Action grants -> the compiler-derived Action allowlist;
- explicit Object read/export/CRUD grants -> their own scoped grants;
- eligible relation fields -> exact source/field/target reference policies;
- Report and Export Control sources -> their validated functional/data closure.

The compiled Blueprint and Runtime Manifest contain only
`permissions[].permission_key/data_scope/audit_denial` for Role authorization.

A Handler-written Object is `action_only`. Its allowed roles explicitly grant
the same-key Action Permission, but do not receive direct CRUD mutation
permissions. Authoring such a direct permission is a blocking write-owner
conflict.

Field, export and guardrail policies remain explicit business exceptions and
use keyed maps wherever their schema has stable identity. Reference policies
are compiler-owned because relation target and role access are already known.
Custom data predicates are not part of role authoring. If none of the five
canonical scopes expresses the requirement, stop and surface a contract gap;
do not invent a sixth value or embed a predicate:

```json
{"roles": {"work_operator": ["work_item.read;owner"]}}
```

## Runtime ownership and verification

At apply, Plane publishes the generated project role catalog. Identity stores
current users and role assignments. Runtime evaluates the resolved principal,
exact scoped grant, field/reference policy and export policy on every
request.

Scope enforcement is storage-bound. For `all`, SQL keeps workspace, caller
filters and target IDs but adds no data-scope predicate. For the other four
values, list/read SQL combines the compiled scope predicate with caller filters;
update/delete/restore first select the requested single ID or bounded ID batch
within that scope, then retain the same predicate on the atomic mutation. Mixed
allowed/out-of-scope batches fail and roll back.
Application-side filtering of unscoped rows is never sufficient evidence.

Verification uses SDK-backed principals created through the supported Identity
test path:

- positive cases prove the exact Permission grant and matching `data_scope`;
- function-denied cases omit the permission or assignment;
- row-denied cases target a record outside the selected scope;
- rejected mutations prove durable state did not change;
- field/reference/export cases assert their exact masking or denial.

Never paste an SDK `AccessBundle`, `FunctionGrant`, or `DataPolicy` into
`backend/model/*.json`, and never provision a Blueprint user just to make a
test executable.
# Project role and data-scope cookbook

The backend model defines business roles and a scope on every exact Permission;
Plane derives reference policies;
Identity owns users and live role assignments.

Use exactly these scopes. Choose from the business ownership boundary, not from
the screen name or the role's seniority:

| Scope | Runtime row boundary | Use it for | Do not use it for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | No additional data-scope predicate inside the current workspace. Workspace, caller filter and target-ID predicates still apply. | A workspace-wide responsibility, such as a central finance operator processing every invoice, an auditor reading every business record, or a shared catalog maintained for the whole workspace. | A convenient default when ownership is unclear, or access intended to cross workspace boundaries. |
| `owner` | `owner_user_id == current subject ID`. | Individually owned work, such as a salesperson's assigned leads, a member's own profile or booking, or a handler that may update only the target record assigned to its actor. | “Created by me” unless creator and current owner are deliberately the same fact; team, manager-reporting-line, or organization access. |
| `org` | `owner_org_id == current subject org ID`. | One-node organization responsibility, such as store staff operating only their own store's orders or a department clerk handling only that department's requests. | Regional managers who also need descendant organizations, or support staff serving another organization. |
| `org_child` | `owner_org_id` is in the Identity-issued current-organization subtree (`org_scope_ids`). | Hierarchical line responsibility, such as a regional manager seeing the region plus child stores, or a division operator processing its departments' records. | Direct-report/team membership—the scope follows the organization tree, not the personnel reporting line—or a separately supported target organization. |
| `target_org` | `owner_org_id` is in the Identity-issued trusted support-organization subtree (`support_org_scope_ids`). | Cross-organization service responsibility, such as a shared-service or customer-support agent whose real home organization remains unchanged but who is assigned to serve a sales/customer organization and its descendants. | Arbitrary cross-organization access, the actor's home organization tree, or an organization ID selected from the request. Without a trusted support assignment the scope matches no rows. |

Apply the choice independently to every exact Action Permission. A role may,
for example, read all department requests with `org_child` but approve only
personally assigned requests with `owner`. For scoped create or reassignment,
the resulting Runtime-owned `owner_user_id` or `owner_org_id` must remain inside
that Permission's selected boundary.

## `target_org` functional-service patterns

Use `target_org` when a functional-service actor keeps one real home
organization but is responsible for data owned by another business
organization subtree. Keep the current contract names distinct:

- `org_id` is the user's real primary organization;
- `support_org_id` is the optional Identity-managed root of the business
  organization subtree that the user serves;
- Identity validates that root and derives it plus its active descendants into
  the trusted `support_org_scope_ids` principal fact;
- `target_org` is the data-scope value on each exact Permission and compiles to
  the derived support subtree.

There is no `target_org_id` field. Do not change the user's primary `org_id`,
attach the user to a manager account or Role, copy organization paths into
business records, or author live user bindings in the backend model. The
Identity administrator assigns `support_org_id` to an active organization-unit
node.

### Customer service reading sales-owned customers

Assume customer records are owned by the sales organization through their
Runtime `owner_org_id`. A customer-service agent belongs to the Customer
Service organization, so `org` and `org_child` correctly provide no customer
access. Keep the agent's `org_id` as Customer Service, set `support_org_id` to
the organization-unit node led by the responsible Sales Manager or Sales
Director (or another truthful sales-region root), and grant only the needed
exact Action:

```json
{"customer_service": ["customer.read;target_org"]}
```

The agent can then read customers whose `owner_org_id` belongs to that sales
subtree. This does not grant `customer.update`, export, or any other Action, and
does not make Customer Service the owner of those customers. “One agent serves
many customers” is represented by those customers' sales-owner nodes falling
under the assigned support subtree, not by listing customer IDs on the user.

### HR account administration for different operating teams

Assume two HR account administrators both belong to an HR operations
organization, but one manages Customer Service accounts and the other manages
Sales accounts. Keep both administrators' real `org_id` in HR. Assign the first
administrator's `support_org_id` to the Customer Service organization root and
the second administrator's to the Sales organization root. Give each HR role
the exact Identity Actions required by the workflow, for example:

```json
{"scoped_account_admin": [
  "identity.organization_units.list;target_org",
  "identity.users.list;target_org",
  "identity.users.get;target_org",
  "identity.users.create;target_org"
]}
```

Identity then returns organization nodes whose IDs are in that administrator's
support subtree, returns users whose `org_id` is in the same subtree, and
rejects creation of a user whose `org_id` falls outside it. Add update, disable,
role-assignment, credential or security Actions only when the requirements call
for them; list/create scope never implies those grants.

The current user model has one `support_org_id`, so it expresses one connected
organization subtree. If one actor must serve several unrelated roots, do not
silently use `all` or invent a list-valued field: use a truthful common parent
node when the organization model has one, otherwise surface a contract gap.

There is no `none` or `custom` scope. Absence of an exact Permission grant means deny.
This example scopes member records to Runtime-maintained ownership:

```json
{
  "objects": {
    "gym_member": {
      "fields": {
        "identity_user_id": "relation!->identity_user;unique",
        "status": "select![active:有效|frozen:冻结]=active"
      }
    },
    "booking": {"fields": {"member_id": "relation!->gym_member"}}
  },
  "roles": {
    "member": ["gym_member.read;owner", "booking.read;owner", "booking.create;owner"],
    "front_desk": ["gym_member.read;all", "booking.read;all", "booking.update;all"]
  },
  "entrypoints": {
    "member_booking": {
	  "audience": "consumer",
      "primary_object": "booking",
      "read_objects": ["gym_member", "booking"],
      "create_objects": ["booking"]
    },
    "front_desk": {
	  "audience": "internal",
      "primary_object": "booking",
      "read_objects": ["gym_member", "booking"],
      "update_objects": ["booking"]
    }
  }
}
```

Plane preserves every exact scoped grant. Runtime exposes an entrypoint only
when the exact Permission and its row scope pass. Tests provision real Identity principals and prove positive,
function-denied and out-of-scope cases, including unchanged durable state after
rejected writes.

Never author Identity users, assignments, SDK access bundles, ownership system
columns, wildcard permissions or an application-side authorization service.

# Domainry Plane boundary

V2 uses Domainry Plane only through the single packaged `domainry-cli` executable.

Choose one explicit `--environment <local|dev|stage|online>` or `--service <url>` target for `apply model` and Connector definition discovery. Keep that target fixed for the batch.

Release only with:

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> [one target]
```

The command converges `backend/model/*.json`, checks the complete model, validates it with Domainry Plane, publishes the immutable delivery, and materializes or evolves the backend. Source preparation, implementation, tests, and `apply finalize` follow explicitly in the same apply stage. For an existing Builder delivery change, inspect the first run's immutable evolution audit, then rerun the same product command with `--evolution-audit-sha256 <emitted-sha256> --evolution-reason <reviewed-reason>`. A stale audit fails closed. Repair any other failed input or stage before rerunning the direct command.

Do not call Domainry Plane directly, reconstruct signing, hand-edit delivery state, or invent separate validate/publish/materialize commands. The current Builder flow keeps reviewed evolution inside `apply model`; it exposes no neighboring delivery-maintenance command surface.
# Authorization and behavior ownership

Keep Action invocation, exact Permission grants, field policy, frontend
navigation, assurance and execution ownership separate.

In backend-model V3:

- the Role's exact `<action_key>;<data_scope>` array entry is the single
  authored Handler allowlist. Never write `Action.roles` or
  `authorization.allowed_roles`; Plane reverse-derives both the allowlist and
  the complete internal authorization contract from Role grants.
- `handler.access` is the minimum Object/operation EffectAuthority. Do not also
  write `handler.data_access`.
- an ordinary Role is an array of exact `<permission_key>;<data_scope>` strings;
  each Action or CRUD Permission has its own `data_scope`.
- Plane derives the Action Permission definition, reference policies, Handler
  EffectAuthority, behavior tuple and Object write policy. It never invents a
  Role grant or scope value.

```json
{
  "roles": {
    "case_reviewer": ["case.read;org", "case.approve;owner"]
  },
  "actions": {
    "case.approve": {
      "kind": "record_operation",
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Approval verifies eligibility and records a durable decision",
        "access": {
          "case": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
          "case_decision": ["create"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Read operations are `get`, `get_for_update`, `optional`, `list`, `exists`, and
`count`. Write operations are `create`, `update`, `conditional_update`,
`delete`, and `restore`. Locking is not mutation authority. Existing-record
update/delete/restore requires `get_for_update` or `conditional_update`.

Use `object_operation` when no existing record target is supplied and
`record_operation` for a routed record target. Route record ID, workspace,
principal, request, trace and idempotency identities are Runtime/protocol
context and are rejected as Action business input.

A Handler-written Object is `action_only`; its allowed role must explicitly
hold the Handler Action's same-key scoped grant but no direct CRUD permission.
Every other Object is `direct_crud`. Never widen a role or add direct CRUD
merely to satisfy a Handler.

## Scope is an SQL mutation boundary

Treat data-scope enforcement as part of the repository operation, not as
response filtering. `all` means no additional data-scope `WHERE`; workspace,
caller filters and target IDs remain mandatory. Generated reads for `owner`,
`org`, `org_child` and `target_org` must combine the compiled predicate with
those conditions. Existing-record update, delete and restore capabilities must
first select the requested single ID or bounded ID batch with the same scope,
then execute the mutation with that predicate still present in its `UPDATE` or
`DELETE`. Batch target counts must match the authorized selection; any missing
or out-of-scope target fails the whole transaction without partial writes.

Never satisfy scope acceptance by loading unscoped rows and filtering them in
project code. Tests must prove an allowed ID succeeds, an out-of-scope ID is
unchanged, mixed allowed/denied batches roll back atomically, and the repository
query/mutation carries the compiled non-`all` predicate or proves that `all`
contains only workspace, caller-filter and target-ID conditions.

Organization claims are trusted Runtime facts,
not request fields or guessed headers. Sensitive fields remain fail-closed and
their explicit policy comes from the active Authoring Definition.

After implementation, map confirmed PRD authorization boundaries to focused
business-flow tests: actor, target, expected grant/scope, result or denial, and
unchanged durable state after rejection. Use real Identity-backed principals;
Blueprint declarations are not assignment evidence.
# Backend Runtime integration and managed proof

This reference covers the closed Runtime HTTP boundary, Action invocation, managed Runtime proof, and backend Handler coding idioms. Capability discovery comes from the CLI-compiled authority contract. Frontend dependency installation and package wiring remain outside this Skill except for the authorized Data Exchange export-center integration.

## Closed HTTP boundary

Project-owned backend source must not add, register, proxy, or require any application-facing HTTP interface. Do not create a project-local HTTP handler, router, controller, middleware endpoint, API facade, API proxy, serverless function, or alternate transport route. The authorized export center may wire only typed operations already published by the Application Delivery `runtime-domain-api-v1` contract; a missing Data Exchange job-list operation is a platform-owner gap, never permission to add or guess a route.

Custom source-owned Action Handlers expose no separate HTTP route; Runtime invokes them only through the published object or record Action operations below. Connector providers may perform contract-declared outbound calls through generated Connector APIs and governed transport, but they must not publish an inbound project API. If the published Runtime CRUD, Action, Report, file, authentication, or Connector contracts cannot express a required behavior, record the exact platform-owner finding and repair that owner in the same session instead of adding an HTTP endpoint; only the terminal policy's proved unrecoverable conditions permit stopping.

## Action invocation

Select object versus record invocation from the Runtime-published Action `kind`, using `runtimeActionInvocationScope`; never infer it from UI layout or from whether the execution owner is a custom Handler.

- `object_create`, `object_operation`, and `bulk_operation` use `runObjectAction` at `POST /records/{objectKey}/actions/{actionKey}`.
- `record_update`, `record_delete`, `record_restore`, `transition_state`, `conditional_update`, and `record_operation` use `runRecordAction` at `POST /records/{objectKey}/items/{recordID}/actions/{actionKey}`.

Business-flow tests wrap typed Action input as `{"data": <payload>}`; a bare payload is invalid for the Action invocation contract.

Call `listActions(objectKey)` first and pass the returned full `action_definition.key` unchanged to `runObjectAction` or `runRecordAction`; never shorten `group_class.book_group_class` to `book_group_class`. Use the exact storage values published by the Action input contract, such as `member`, not translated labels such as `会员`. A `record_operation` also requires the existing record ID in the record route; the presence of a button on an object list does not turn it into an object Action.

Frontends never call a generated Handler directly. Preserve the bounded Action input/output contract, workspace, bearer identity, request ID, idempotency key, assurance token, and concurrency value. Preserve Runtime result references and triggered workflows instead of reducing the response to a success boolean.

One accepted business intent must produce one Runtime mutation request. For example, “open table” is one declared Action call, not `create table session` followed by separate status, occupancy, audit, and notification mutations. Do not use `Promise.all`, sequential mutation hooks, retries with new keys, or a browser-side rollback to assemble one atomic backend command. Put the complete typed input on the Action and let its Runtime-owned unit of work perform all effects. Refetch/invalidation after the response and polling a returned job are allowed reads; they must not hide additional writes.

## Managed Runtime proof

Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify --json --project <project> --address 127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>`. It verifies and packages the project, starts the exact package to healthy state, stops it, restarts the same package/database cohort to healthy state, and finally stops it. A failure triggers best-effort cleanup of any Runtime started by that invocation. If it fails, remain in `verify`, repair the named owner, and rerun the same command. Never background-launch, discover arbitrary PIDs, kill unrelated processes, or add a separate Runtime-control step.

Runtime proof must cover declared allowed, denied, and scoped actors; Action effects; conditional conflicts; transaction rollback; idempotent replay without a second mutation or receipt; workflows/outbox; durable audit; and current delivery/package/Runtime receipt identity. `backend/tests/businessflow` is black-box: use only published Runtime HTTP/client operations, never direct project Handler calls, generated capability/data fakes, or database access. The managed child environment publishes the opaque workspace, application, management login, initial password and independent changed password under `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_*`; use the mandatory initial password-change flow and never scrape logs or reuse another cohort's identity. Use task-published database evidence paths only for owner diagnostics; project business-flow tests do not open them or rediscover private schema.

A common login/read/catalog helper proves only that common precondition. Each case must then execute the Runtime operation sequence named by its requirement and read back its own terminal result. Human approval proof uses the declared Workflow process/task surfaces and both approved/rejected outcomes; calling approve/reject Handlers directly is not Workflow proof. Governed Report export proof uses Report query/prepare plus the requester-owned Data Exchange job and completed download, including unauthorized-role and cross-requester denial; a Report definition plus `*.export` permission is not export-control proof.

Successful `verify` returns `verified_and_stopped`; a running process, local HTTP response, or browser screenshot without matching delivery, package, database-cohort, and Runtime identity is not release evidence.

## Handler coding idioms (validated against the live Runtime)

These are Runtime-facing Handler constraints. `apply finalize` statically checks capability I/O in loops/recursion, bounded List pagination, handled capability results, and each `ConditionalUpdate` call's actual mutation argument. Unit and Runtime tests still own business semantics.

**Finalizer source-contract preflight.** Keep generated capability I/O outside loops and recursive cycles: select into bounded slices, build batch inputs in pure loops, and invoke each generated batch/query capability once. Every List query uses `Page(page, pageSize)` with literal `pageSize` in `1..200`. Handle every result and error. Batch inputs are `1..200`, ordered one-to-one, and inherit the Action Workspace, Principal, grants, Scope, and transaction. Minimal shape:

```go
// Pure selection: capability I/O only outside loops.
orders, err := caps.RepairOrder.List(ctx, data.NewRepairOrderQuery().
    WhereStatusEqual(schema.RepairOrderStatusDispatched).
    OrderByIDAscending().
    Page(1, 200)) // literal page size, 1..200
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
pending := make([]schema.RepairOrder, 0, runCapacity)
for _, order := range orders { // pure filtering loop: no capability calls here
    if len(pending) == runCapacity {
        break
    }
    if eligible(order) {
        pending = append(pending, order)
    }
}
queries := make([]data.DispatchReceiptQuery, len(pending))
for index, order := range pending { // pure request construction only
    queries[index] = data.NewDispatchReceiptQuery().
        WhereOrderIDEqual(order.ID).
        WhereBusinessDateEqual(businessDate)
}
exists, err := caps.DispatchReceipt.ExistsBatch(ctx, queries) // one call, outside loops
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
// Build CreateBatch and notification DispatchBatch inputs in pure loops, then
// invoke each batch once outside loops and return every error unchanged.
```

**Build tag.** Backend compile requires the Domain SDK build constraint: a plain `go build ./...` fails on `verifiedDomainSDKBuildConstraint`. The tag is published as `schema.DomainSDKBuildConstraint` in the generated schema package's revision constants; run all backend commands as `go build|vet|test -tags "$(go run ./cmd/... 2>/dev/null || grep -roh 'domainry_domain_sdk_[a-f0-9]*' backend/generated/ | head -1)" ./...` — or read the constant from `backend/generated/schema/revision.gen.go`. The CLI's `verify` command supplies the tag automatically; only manual Go commands need it.

**ConditionalUpdate requires a real condition.** Attach the compare-and-set condition observed under `GetForUpdate`; `apply finalize` checks the mutation argument at every call site:

```go
mutation := data.NewTicketUpdate(ticket.ID).SetAssigneeID(assignee)
if ticket.AssigneeID == nil {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDNull("ticket.assign.conflict")
} else {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDEqual(*ticket.AssigneeID, "ticket.assign.conflict")
}
updated, err := caps.Ticket.ConditionalUpdate(ctx, mutation)
```

`Require<Field>Equal/NotEqual/Null(errorCode)`, `WithExpectedUpdatedAt(...)`, and arithmetic `Increment*`/`Decrement*` effects satisfy the generated condition contract. Scaffolded or hand-written fakes must call `ValidateConditionalMutation`. On idempotent replay the predicate may legitimately differ; assert each execution's expected mutation rather than byte equality.

**NotificationIntent.SubjectVersion must be non-empty.** `runtimeext.NotificationIntent` fails `backend.notification.action_intent_invalid` when `SubjectVersion` is empty. Generated typed reads and mutation results expose `UpdatedAt`; mutation results receive it from the same canonical staged commit that Runtime persists. Use the subject record's `UpdatedAt` (including the value returned by `ConditionalUpdate`) as `SubjectVersion`; do not substitute transport metadata such as `request_id`, leave the field empty, or skip the dispatch.

**Transition Actions from Handlers or probes** must send the target state in the request payload (see `crud-and-state-machine.md`): a payload-less transition fails closed with 400 `backend.action.transition_payload_required`.
# Project-owned source

Git owns project source. Edit, format, test, rename, and delete in-scope project source with normal development tools while preserving unrelated work. Treat a canonical Handler and its paired test as one review unit and keep both aligned with the same implementation-packet entry. `frontend/**` remains read-only except when an exportable Object SQL Report requires the Data Exchange export center and the TODO says `Frontend mutation scope: integration_authorized`; evidence that assigns any other defect to the frontend produces a finding with owner `frontend`, never an edit.

Allowed backend source includes `backend/go.mod`, `backend/go.sum`, `backend/actions/**`, `backend/config/**`, `backend/connectors/**`, `backend/domain/**`, `backend/i18n/**`, and `backend/tests/**`. The sole frontend allowance is the existing project's route/navigation, feature components, typed-client integration, localization, and focused tests needed for the export center in [offline Report export frontend](frontend-offline-report-export.md); do not mutate unrelated frontend source. Never edit `backend/generated/**`, `backend/cmd/**`, frozen contracts, Runtime manifests, receipts, caches, journals, packages, or other `.domainry/**` state. The only writable `.domainry` exception is the current session's `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md` TODO.

## Normal delivered-batch sequence

This is the only source sequence after `apply model` succeeds:

1. Retain the exact `.implementation_packet.path`, delivery/materialization identity, file hash, and returned `actions[]` direct-path index from `apply model`. That command validates every delivered Action context, creates only missing canonical Handler/test skeletons, and persists immutable content-addressed context files under managed `.domainry/builder/**`.
2. For one Action at a time, find its exact `action_key` in the small returned index and read that entry's `path` directly. The file is already the complete single-Action context, including only its referenced document content; do not run `jq`, open the batch index, reconstruct a document table, use `latest.json`, or read generated capabilities/context files directly.
3. Implement the complete Action-context Handler and paired test directly with normal source-editing tools. If either file changed concurrently, stop and reconcile both against the immutable context before continuing.
4. For an approved Connector source gap, load `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project <project> --connector-context <connector.provider>` immediately before implementing that Connector under `backend/connectors/**`. Action packet context does not replace Connector context.
5. Implement other allowed project-owned backend source/tests and the authorized export-center exception. Run focused tests, then the affected backend test set.
6. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply finalize --json --project <project>` once all implementation TODO items for the materialized delivery are closed.

There is no second prepare, per-Action context, or source-write command.

The batch-prepared skeleton compiles against delivered capability types but intentionally returns `*.not_implemented`. It exposes missing implementation coverage and is never positive-path evidence. Replace the paired generated test's nil Execution call and placeholder oracle with typed non-nil Execution/capability stubs and assertions over current outputs and business effects; a generic no-panic assertion is not meaningful behavior evidence.

## Finalization boundary

After source/tests are implemented and every preceding implementation TODO item is closed, run the exact generated-SDK-tagged focused Go tests, then `apply finalize`. Finalization scans delivery-bound canonical Action source/test paths. A Handler paired with a generated test that still has nil Execution or an exact `*.not_implemented` oracle returns `state:"invalid"`; source-policy and applicable Go compile failures also fail closed. Finalize writes only its failure receipt on failure. Cross-module/full verification, packaging, and Runtime start require the current successful finalization.

# Records, fields, and relations

Runtime owns ordinary record persistence, typed normalization, validation,
references, queries and mutations. The backend model declares only business
Objects and their business fields.

## Compact Object form

```json
{"objects": {
  "invoice": {
    "description": "Customer invoice and governed financial state",
    "fields": {
      "business_no": "text!;unique",
      "status": "select![draft:草稿|issued:已开具]=draft",
      "customer_id": "relation!->customer",
      "amount": "currency!;precision=19;scale=2;currency=CNY;rounding=half_even",
      "discount_rate": "percent;precision=5;scale=2;rounding=half_even",
      "remark": "long_text;max_length=500"
    }
  }
}}
```

Object identity and field identity are their map keys. Plane supplies default
names, required empty config, labeled options and deterministic Object
description when no meaningful explicit description is present.

Supported types are `boolean`, `currency`, `date`, `datetime`, `email`,
`integer`, `long_text`, `number`, `percent`, `phone`, `relation`, `select`,
`text`, `url`, and `user`. `number` is binary floating point. Use `currency` or
`percent` for exact declared-scale values; generated code keeps their canonical
named decimal strings.

Exact values use `precision`, `scale`, `currency`, and `rounding`. `relation`
requires `->target` and cannot have a default. `select` requires a stable,
unique vocabulary; `value:label` carries localized display text without
changing the stored value. Supported validators are `min_length`, `max_length`,
`min`, `max`, and `pattern`. `unique` is a flag with no value.
`indexed` and `localized` are flags. Relation modifiers are `cardinality`,
